chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:
Do not pray in the stalls of horses, mules, and donkeys.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in the stalls of horses and donkeys according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the principle of *istihya* (modesty/shyness) and ritual purity (*taharah*) in prayer spaces, extending the concept of respecting the prayer area to include areas associated with animals. Scholars interpret 'marabit' (stalls/enclosures) as places where animals rest or are tethered, noting that the presence of animals or their waste may introduce impurities (*najis*) or distractions that detract from the reverence (*khushu*) required in *salat*. This ruling reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on maintaining the sanctity and cleanliness of the space designated for communion with Allah.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,
‘Do not pray Salāt in stalls of the cavalry horses, and the mules and the donkeys’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘
You must not perform Salah (prayer) in places where horses, mules and donkeys are kept.’”
